work_order.understanding:
TWO SEPARATE THINGS, and this revision answers both.

FIRST, the plan reviewer's objection was correct and is now fixed by measurement. He wrote that AC-3's added second sentence -- "A subdirectory that cannot be read does not change this: only the top-level directory's own absence yields exactly one line" -- asserts an exclusivity the prescribed fix does not have. I reproduced his objection exactly rather than taking it on trust: with the fixed collectFailures, a notes directory holding ONE chmod-000 subdirectory and otherwise-VALID notes returns exactly ONE string ('cannot read <dir>/locked: EACCES ...'), length 1. The onError callback contributes one 'cannot read' string and the notes outside it contribute zero, so case B does print exactly one line. AC-3 is rewritten below to scope the guarantee -- a missing/unreadable TOP-LEVEL directory yields exactly one string; an unreadable SUBdirectory yields its own 'cannot read' string ALONGSIDE every failure of the notes outside it, so exactly one line only when those other notes are clean -- and the same rule is mirrored word for word into AC-10's how_to_verify. The 'does not change this' framing and the exclusivity claim are both gone.

SECOND, and this is the diagnosis the previous attempt got wrong. It said its root cause was RIGHT because QA confirmed the headline fix real -- all eight original criteria pass; a nested note now reaches the changelog and the generated docs page (QA's T-11 shows the marker on the page). That much is true and stays true. But the previous attempt carried a premise it never examined: it treated 'the two sides must agree on WHICH files exist' as the whole invariant, and asserted that a nested README.md being validated as a note is 'the correct outcome of that shared rule, not a bug to route around'. Unifying the enumeration was necessary but not sufficient. The gate and the publisher now agree on the file SET and disagree on what happens when a member of that set is malformed. The gate (validateNote) turns every malformation into a named failure string and keeps going; the publisher (parseReleaseNotes) dereferences data.authors unguarded and dies. That asymmetry was harmless while the publisher only read top-level files the gate had already cleared -- an invariant the recursive walk breaks, because gate and publisher now agree a NESTED file is a note and the publisher has no validateNote equivalent. The root cause is a behaviour-parity gap, not an enumeration gap.

I reproduced all three bugs myself against d4684c80 in a worktree at that commit, and then prototyped all three fixes against the real modules. BUG-1: parseReleaseNotes throws 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading map)' on a note with no authors list. BUG-2: collectFailures wraps the ENTIRE recursive walk in one try/catch, so one chmod-000 subdirectory discards every failure already accumulated. BUG-3: the new guard in release-notes-check.mjs calls reportError from module scope, but reportError only exits synchronously when GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is ABSENT -- the one environment a real Actions runner never has and the one the unit harness deletes. All 83 existing tests pass on that commit; nothing here is a red suite, all three bugs sit outside coverage.

One further finding the previous attempt did not have: its BUG-2 fix text said 'path is already imported at the top of the file', but following that literally as a bare join(dir, relative) crashes with 'ReferenceError: join is not defined' -- release-notes-gate.mjs imports * as path and has no bare join binding. The change text below names path.join explicitly.
work_order.root_cause: The shared walk made the gate and the publisher agree on WHICH files are release notes, but nothing made them agree on WHAT a malformed member of that set does. release-notes-gate.mjs's validateNote turns every rule violation into a named failure string and keeps going; parseReleaseNotes has no equivalent and dereferences data.authors.map with no Array.isArray guard. Before this PR that was latent, because the publisher only ever read top-level files the gate had already cleared. The recursive walk routed nested files into it, so the pre-existing unguarded dereference became reachable. Two smaller instances of the same 'report, do not abort and do not discard' rule were broken by this PR's own additions: collectFailures' single try/catch around the whole walk converts a partial walk into a total one (a throw at depth N discards depths 0..N-1), and reportError defers process.exit to a WriteStream 'close' event whenever GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is set, so it is not a terminating function on the only platform it runs on.
work_order.approach:
Three targeted repairs, each making one participant obey the rule the other two already follow. Nothing about the enumeration changes and none of the eight original acceptance criteria is rewritten -- all eight pass today and pass again with every fix below applied.

BUG-1: guard the dereference in parseReleaseNotes with Array.isArray(data.authors), and on failure THROW an Error naming the note's path relative to the notes directory. Throwing rather than skipping is load-bearing and I verified the mechanism this time rather than reasoning about it: release-notes-generate.mjs awaits parseReleaseNotes at line 146, long before the `files.map(f => fs.unlink(...))` at line 264, and `files` comes from listNotePaths regardless of whether the note parsed.

BUG-2: move the try/catch INSIDE the walk via an optional onError callback on listNotePaths; with no callback the walk rethrows exactly as today. collectFailures passes a callback accumulating a 'cannot read <path>: <message>' per unreadable directory and returns those alongside, not instead of, the per-note failures. Two details the previous attempt left open and this one settles: use path.join(dir, relative), NOT a bare join(...), and SORT the accumulated unreadable array before concatenating, because those entries arrive in readdir order -- the filesystem's, not ours -- and AC-7 requires a report order that does not shift between contributors' machines.

BUG-3: make reportError terminating on both paths by replacing the createWriteStream(...).on('close', exit) tail with a synchronous fs.appendFileSync guarded by try/catch, followed by an unconditional process.exit(1). The try/catch is load-bearing: appendFileSync THROWS on an unwritable summary path. I verified all four env shapes against the real script.

The harness is what let BUG-3 hide, and this is the part the plan reviewer caught. runCheck gains an optional second parameter for env overrides, applied AFTER `const env = { ...process.env, BASE_REF: BASE_BRANCH }`, treating an undefined value as a DELETE rather than stringifying it. The new BUG-3 case MUST pass `BASE_REF: undefined`. I measured both variants against the UNFIXED script rather than arguing about them: with the previous order's prescribed call (BASE_REF left set by the harness) the case PASSES 85/85 -- vacuous, exactly as he said; with the corrected call it FAILS (1 failed, 84 passed) and passes once the fix is applied.

Every new case is falsifiability-checked by reverting its source fix and recording the failure, not merely recorded green.

files.change: In parseReleaseNotes, immediately after `const { data, content: body } = matter(content);` and before the `data.authors.map` call, insert a guard: `if (!Array.isArray(data.authors)) throw new Error(...)` whose message names the note by its path relative to the notes directory (`name` is already in scope). Do NOT skip the file instead of throwing -- release-notes-generate.mjs unlinks every path in the returned `files` array at its line 264, and `files` comes from listNotePaths regardless of whether the note parsed. In listNotePaths, add a second optional parameter `onError` and move the directory read inside the recursion into a try/catch: on failure, `if (onError) { onError(prefix, error); return; }` and otherwise `throw error`.
files.why: BUG-1's crash and BUG-2's discarded failures both live in this file. BUG-1 is the only defect whose blast radius is an aborted release.

files.change: Forward the new parameter through the exported listNotePaths wrapper. Rewrite collectFailures to stop wrapping the whole walk: declare `const unreadable = []`, pass a callback that pushes `cannot read ${prefix ? path.join(dir, prefix) : dir}: ${error.message}`, then return `[...unreadable.sort(), ...paths.flatMap(...) ]`. Two things are load-bearing: use `path.join`, NOT a bare `join(...)` (this file imports `* as path` and has no bare `join` binding, so `join(dir, prefix)` is a ReferenceError), and SORT `unreadable` before concatenating, carrying the same oxlint-disable comment the walk's own sort carries.
files.why: Closes BUG-2 while leaving the gate's public surface and AC-3's missing-directory shape exactly as they are.

files.change: In reportError, replace the `if (!process.env.GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY) { process.exit(1); }` early return followed by the createWriteStream(...).on('close', exit) tail with a `try { fs.appendFileSync(...) } catch {}` guarded by `if (process.env.GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY)`, then an unconditional `process.exit(1)`. Rewrite the comment above it, which currently claims the runner always supplies GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and that without it there is nothing left to do but exit -- after this change both branches do the same thing, and that comment is what made the defect invisible.
files.why: BUG-3. The guard is correct in intent and wrong in mechanism: it called a function that returns instead of exiting on every real Actions run, so the BASE_REF check below it kept executing.

files.change: Add a describe block covering the publisher's malformed-input path, which had no coverage at all -- that is why BUG-1 reached a PR. Use fs.mkdtempSync under os.tmpdir() and mock console.log the way the existing block does. Add a second describe block for the onError callback asserting the callback fires AND that the returned array still holds both the top-level note and the readable nested note -- that second half is the regression BUG-2 was. Skip the permission cases under root.
files.why: The publisher's malformed-input path had no coverage at all, which is why BUG-1 reached a PR.

files.change: Give runCheck an optional second parameter for extra/overridden child env entries, merged AFTER `const env = { ...process.env, BASE_REF: BASE_BRANCH }`, with an undefined value DELETING the key rather than stringifying it. The new BUG-3 case MUST pass `BASE_REF: undefined`: measured, the previous order's call without it passes 85/85 against the unfixed script, and the corrected call fails it. Add collectFailures cases for BUG-2, for AC-3's one-string shape, and for the deterministic order of the unreadable entries.
files.why: BUG-3 is invisible to the suite precisely because runCheck deletes the variable that makes the new code misbehave, AND injects BASE_REF which hides the symptom.

These five changed files are .mjs CLI tooling with no UI surface, so every case above is exercised with node rather than a browser, and each should cite a saved exchange
risks: The BUG-1 guard makes parseReleaseNotes throw a plain Error where it previously threw a TypeError. Both abort, but a future caller catching TypeError specifically would now catch a plain Error. No such caller exists today.

The throw happens inside files.map(async ...), so Promise.all rejects and the remaining notes are never read. That is the intended abort, but one bad note stops the whole changelog — the correct trade precisely because of the unlink at release-notes-generate.mjs:264, which runs against a `files` array built at line 146.

fs.appendFileSync in reportError is synchronous, so a large README is written on the main thread before exit. The README is small; a pathological one would cost milliseconds. The try/catch is load-bearing, not defensive padding.

Changing collectFailures' return shape from 'either the note failures or the unreadable-directory string' to 'both' means a caller asserting on array length or on [0] would see different output. The only caller is main(), which iterates and prints.

Sorting the unreadable entries changes their order relative to walk order. No criterion or existing test depends on walk order, and AC-7 requires a deterministic order that does not follow readdir — but it is a behaviour change to output that did not exist before this diff.
The chmod-000 cases are meaningless when the suite runs as root, because root ignores the permission bits. Both new permission cases must skip under root.

Making runCheck's env override accept deletions is a small change to a helper thirteen existing cases share. If the merge is placed before the BASE_REF injection rather than after, the deletion has no effect and the new BUG-3 case goes vacuous again — precisely the failure the plan reviewer caught.
out_of_scope: The absolute filesystem path in the ENOENT message is NOT changed. QA graded it a note rather than a defect: the message names the directory it was handed because a fixed string would misreport the tmpdir the unit suite passes.

Windows path separators are NOT addressed. listNotePaths builds relative paths with a literal '/' and joins with node:path.join, so a Windows checkout would produce 'sub\\deep.md' from the join. QA flagged this as an unverified platform risk, this repository's CI is ubuntu-only, and no acceptance criterion claims Windows support.

An unrecognised `category` in a nested note (parseReleaseNotes logs 'WARNING: Unrecognized category') is NOT changed. QA listed it as a coverage gap it did not exercise, it is pre-existing behaviour unrelated to the recursive walk.

release-notes-generate.mjs end to end is NOT driven. It needs a release branch, a version, a slug and a remote. The emptied-subdirectory side effect of unlinking a nested note's file is therefore still unverified by execution.
work_order.confidence_rationale: High because all three bugs were reproduced by me against d4684c80 in a worktree at that commit, all three fixes were prototyped against the real modules, and the full suite is green afterwards, from a floor of 83. The plan reviewer's objection was not argued with but measured: AC-3's exclusive claim is empirically false (case B returns length 1) and AC-3 and AC-10 now say the same rule in the same words. Raised because this revision adds what the last one lacked: a verified-failing BUG-3 case in both harness variants, and a prototype detail (path.join vs a bare join) that would otherwise have cost an implement cycle. Not higher because release-notes-generate.mjs's unlink path is still reasoned from reading the script rather than from running it, even though I confirmed the line numbers that make throw-rather-than-skip load-bearing.
evidence: BUG-1, reproduced by me against d4684c80 in a worktree: a tmpdir holding sub-note.md containing '# no frontmatter'; parseReleaseNotes threw 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading map)'. QA's control shows the same dereference at the top level on the BASE commit, so the missing guard is pre-existing and the walk is what widened its reach.

BUG-2, reproduced by me against d4684c80: a tmpdir holding zzz-broken.md (category Nope, authors [github-actions]) and a chmod-000 subdir/locked. collectFailures returned exactly ['cannot read <dir>: EACCES: permission denied, scandir .../locked'] — both of zzz-broken.md's failures gone. After chmod 755 the same call returned exactly those two failures, proving they were always there and the try/catch discarded them.

BUG-3, reproduced by me against d4684c80, in a throwaway git repo with upcoming-release-notes/ absent: GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY set + BASE_REF unset printed the guard's line and then '::error::BASE_REF env var is not set' (two errors, exit 1, stderr empty). With SUMMARY set + BASE_REF SET it printed only ONE error line — which is exactly why the harness-injected BASE_REF hides the symptom.

THE PLAN REVIEWER'S AC-3 OBJECTION, reproduced rather than conceded: with the fixed collectFailures, a directory holding one chmod-000 subdirectory and otherwise-VALID notes returns exactly ONE string, length 1. So AC-3's previous second sentence was false against the fix that same plan prescribed. AC-3 and AC-10 now state the rule as a scope and qa_script measures the count in both shapes.

THE REVIEWER'S BUG-3 OBJECTION, measured both ways against the UNFIXED check script with the new env-override parameter in place. With the previous order's prescribed call runCheck(repo.dir, { GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY: tmp }) — BASE_REF left set by the harness — the case PASSED 85/85, vacuous, as he said. With the corrected call runCheck(repo.dir, { BASE_REF: undefined, GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY: tmp }) the same case FAILED (1 failed, 84 passed). Restoring the fix, both variants pass and the corrected one reports noBaseLine=true. Node's execFile omits undefined-valued env keys entirely — verified directly — so the deletion is real, not a stringified 'undefined'.

BUG-1 and BUG-2 fixes, prototyped and verified against the real modules: with Array.isArray guarding the dereference, parseReleaseNotes rejected with 'Release note sub/notes.md has no usable `authors` list...' naming the file, and the same guard rejected a bare-string authors while a note WITH authors still published. With the try/catch moved inside the walk behind an onError callback, collectFailures over the locked-dir fixture returned the unreadable entry naming the SUBDIRECTORY plus both note failures in one array, while a missing top-level directory still returned exactly one 'cannot read ...' string.

BUG-3 fix, verified across all four env shapes against the real script: SUMMARY set + BASE_REF unset, SUMMARY set + BASE_REF set, and SUMMARY unset each print exactly one ::error:: line and exit 1; an unwritable SUMMARY path also exits 1 with zero bytes on stderr, which required wrapping appendFileSync in try/catch.

The sort requirement for the new 'cannot read' entries: creating five chmod-000 subdirectories in the order 5,1,3,2,4 and sorting the array returned them 1,2,3,4,5. Without the sort the report order would differ between contributors' machines, which AC-7 forbids.

Non-regression and static checks: with all three prototypes applied, yarn workspace @actual-app/ci-actions run test passed 85/85 across 6 files (83 pre-existing plus the two harness-variant probes), up from the 83/83 floor on d4684c80 with no existing case disturbed. yarn lint reported no errors and 'All matched files use the correct format' across 2546 files. @actual-app/ci-actions typecheck is SKIPPED (all .mjs), so lint is the only static gate here.

QA's report qa-evidence/qa-evidence/qa-report.json, verdict fail on PR #105 at d4684c8, attempt 1: all eight original acceptance criteria pass and the headline fix is confirmed real (T-11 shows the nested note reaching the generated docs page); three bugs recorded — BUG-1 major, BUG-2 and BUG-3 minor — all three reproducible: always and introduced_by_pr: true.

alternatives_considered.approach: For BUG-1, SKIP the malformed note — filter it out of the map and carry on, which is what a publisher arguably wants so one bad note cannot block a release.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It silently loses data. release-notes-generate.mjs unlinks every entry of the returned `files` array at line 264, and `files` comes from listNotePaths at line 146 regardless of whether the note parsed — so a skipped note is deleted from upcoming-release-notes/ and never appears in any changelog. That is this ticket's original defect reappearing one layer down, and it would be invisible in CI because the gate never sees the file. Throwing aborts before the unlink and names the file.

alternatives_considered.approach: For BUG-1, give the publisher the gate's full validateNote and reuse it, so the two participants share one validator as they now share one walk.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: validateNote returns failure strings for a human and takes a dir plus a relative path; parseReleaseNotes needs the parsed data itself to build a changelog entry, not a verdict. Reusing the validator would mean either duplicating the parsing or reshaping validateNote into something neither caller wants. The one Array.isArray guard closes the actual crash at the actual dereference.

alternatives_considered.approach: For BUG-2, keep the single try/catch but have it return the paths accumulated so far alongside the failure string.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The walk builds its result inside a closure over `paths` and a throw discards the function's return value entirely — there is nothing to salvage without restructuring the walk anyway. Catching at the point of failure is both smaller and the only version that keeps reporting later unreadable directories instead of stopping at the first.

alternatives_considered.approach: For BUG-2, leave the unreadable entries in walk order and let the implementer sort them only if AC-7's verification shows instability.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The previous revision deferred this as an unknown, which hands the implementer a judgement call with no failing signal to decide it by — and the three-run check that motivated it was run only on one filesystem, where readdir happened to return creation order. Sorting unconditionally costs one line and makes AC-7 true by construction rather than by luck on ext4.

alternatives_considered.approach: For BUG-3, leave reportError non-terminating and make the module-scope guard set process.exitCode and skip the rest of the file with a guard flag or an early-return wrapper.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It leaves reportError's contract as 'reports and maybe exits', which is the actual defect, and every one of its other seven call sites then has to know whether control really stopped. Making the function terminate unconditionally fixes the class rather than this call site.

alternatives_considered.approach: Flip runCheck's default to SET GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, so all existing subprocess cases exercise the real Actions shape without a new parameter.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It silently redefines what six other assertions were written against, on a fix attempt, with no way to tell from the diff whether a later failure is the fix or the changed baseline. An explicit per-case override makes the environment difference visible in the test that depends on it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Satisfy the BUG-3 requirement without touching runCheck's env construction: have the new case delete BASE_REF by mutating process.env around the runCheck call.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would work, but it mutates the ambient environment of the whole vitest process to express one child variable, and the deletion would then be undone or not depending on which test runs next. An explicit override parameter is a three-line change confined to the helper that already owns the child env.

assumptions: A release note that reaches the publisher without valid front matter indicates the gate was bypassed or bypassed after the fact, not that the publisher should tolerate it. This is why BUG-1's message tells the reader the gate rejects such a note.

parseReleaseNotes has no equivalent of the gate's 'report every problem in one run' contract, so throwing is the only signal available to it. Adding a failure-collecting return shape would change what both callers destructure.

release-notes-generate.mjs:264's unlink of every path in `files` applies to nested paths too, since `files` entries are relative and joined against the notes directory. I confirmed by reading the script that the parse at line 146 precedes the unlink at line 264, which is what makes skipping unsafe for BUG-1.

A real GitHub Actions runner always has GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY set, which is what makes BUG-3 a live defect rather than a local-only one. QA confirmed the variable's presence changes the printed output at d4684c80, and I reproduced both shapes myself.
unknowns: Whether readdir order for the unreadable entries was ever stable across filesystems. It no longer matters for the report, because collectFailures now sorts them — but the answer would have determined whether the sort was needed, and it is unknown.

Whether release-notes-generate.mjs's unlink leaves an emptied subdirectory behind when a nested note is published. Nothing in this attempt executes that script, so it stays a listed risk rather than a verified property.
residual_risks: release-notes-generate.mjs is still never executed end to end — it needs a release branch, a version, a slug and a remote, and it writes into packages/docs/blog and packages/docs/docs/releases.md. The nested unlink path and the emptied-subdirectory side effect remain unverified by execution.

.github/scripts/count-points.mjs is not executed: it is a forbidden path for this ticket and it needs GitHub API credentials. Its glob was read and matches the shared walk's rule, but agreement is by inspection only.
The Windows path-separator disagreement between the walk's literal '/' and path.join's '\\' is unaddressed and unexercised — this runner is Linux and the repository's CI is ubuntu-only.
The gate's `Validated N release note(s)` count printed by main() is not asserted by any criterion, deliberately: a count-based criterion is how PR #91's AC-5 nearly failed a passing change.
@actual-app/ci-actions has no typecheck coverage (every file is .mjs and the task is skipped), so none of these changes is checked by a type checker.

review.title: The ENOENT guard in release-notes-check.mjs does not stop the script in the shape CI runs it. reportError only calls process.exit(1) synchronously when GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is unset; when it is set — always true on a GitHub Actions runner — it opens a write stream and returns, deferring the exit to the stream's close event. Execution falls through the new try/catch into the BASE_REF handling and the async git IIFE. A missing notes directory still runs a network `git fetch` and `git diff`, then prints a SECOND, misleading ::error:: line claiming no release note was added — the opposite diagnosis from the one the guard just reported.
review.detail:
The ENOENT guard in release-notes-check.mjs does not stop the script in the shape CI runs it. reportError only calls process.exit(1) synchronously when GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is unset; when it is set — always true on a GitHub Actions runner — it opens a write stream and returns, deferring the exit to the stream's close event. Execution falls through the new try/catch into the BASE_REF handling and the async git IIFE. A missing notes directory still runs a network `git fetch` and `git diff`, then prints a SECOND, misleading ::error:: line claiming no release note was added — the opposite diagnosis from the one the guard just reported.

`packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs:20`

Evidence: Ran the PR's script against a throwaway repo with upcoming-release-notes/ removed, CI shape (GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY set, BASE_REF set), with a PATH shim logging git invocations:
::error::Cannot read upcoming-release-notes/: ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '.../upcoming-release-notes'
::notice::
::error::No release note added or modified under upcoming-release-notes/. Add a *.md file describing your change, or edit an existing note.
::notice::
--- git invoked after the guard ---
GIT fetch origin base
GIT diff --name-status -z --diff-filter=AMR origin/base...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/
With a normally-fast summary file the stream closes before `git fetch` returns and only one error line appears (5/5 runs), but `git fetch` is still spawned every time — verified against a valid origin, which logged `GIT fetch origin base`. With an unreachable origin and a blocked summary the script dies with an unhandled-rejection stack trace (exit 124 under timeout), the exact output AC-4 says is fixed. The new test cannot catch this: runCheck (release-notes-check.test.mjs:76-81) does `delete env.GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` before spawning, so AC-4's only coverage runs the branch where the guard works.

Fix: Make the guard terminate rather than rely on reportError's deferred exit: move the `Looking in` probe into the async IIFE and `return` from it on failure (the shape the rest of the file already uses), or set a module-level flag and process.exit(1) after the reportError call. Add a test case that runs runCheck with GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY pointed at a real file so the CI shape is covered.

review.title: parseReleaseNotes crashes with an unhandled TypeError on any enumerated note lacking an `authors` key, because data.authors.map(...) at line 217 is unguarded. This is pre-existing for a malformed top-level note, but the recursive walk newly widens the set of files that reach it: a contributor who drops prose documentation at upcoming-release-notes/<team>/README.md — the most natural reason to create a subdirectory there — was invisible to the publisher before and now takes down both release-notes-generate.mjs and packages/docs/scripts/generate-upcoming-release-notes.mjs, which runs before every docs build and start.

`packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs:186`

Evidence: With upcoming-release-notes/team-a/README.md holding plain prose (no front matter) in a worktree of the PR branch:
$ node --input-type=module -e "import {parseReleaseNotes} from '.../util.mjs'; await parseReleaseNotes(...)"
THREW: TypeError Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')
    at util.mjs:217:20
The gate catches the same input cleanly (::error::team-a/README.md is missing a category / is missing authors, EXIT=1), so it can never merge; the exposure is a contributor's local docs build. Confirmed pre-existing at top level: on origin/main's util.mjs a top-level upcoming-release-notes/loose.md with no front matter throws the identical TypeError.

Fix: Either make parseReleaseNotes skip (with a console.log WARNING) any note whose front matter has no `authors`, matching validateNote's graceful handling, or exclude README.md at every level. The work order explicitly deferred the nested-README rule as a product decision, so this is worth a follow-up rather than blocking.

The positive assertion on line 220 is what makes the case meaningful; the negative one reads as coverage of the stack-trace claim while providing none.

`packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.test.mjs:221`

Evidence: Ran the new case against unfixed sources (util.mjs, release-notes-gate.mjs, release-notes-check.mjs reverted to origin/main; tests kept at PR head). The unfixed script does print the ENOENT stack trace — to stderr, so captured stdout is empty and the failure lands on line 220 instead:
AssertionError: expected '' to contain '::error::Cannot read upcoming-release…'
    220|     expect(stdout).toContain('::error::Cannot read upcoming-release-no…')
    221|     expect(stdout).not.toContain('ENOENT: no such file or directory, r…')
Empty stdout means line 221 asserts '' does not contain a substring — true for every possible input.

Fix: Have runCheck also return error.stderr and assert on that (e.g. expect(stderr).not.toContain('ENOENT') and not.toContain('at file:')), or drop line 221 and let the positive assertion carry the case.

review.title: The ENOENT guard in collectFailures names the top-level directory even when the path it could not read is a subdirectory. readdirSync recurses, so an unreadable subdirectory aborts the whole walk and the failure string reads `cannot read <top dir>: ... EACCES ... scandir '<top dir>/<actual culprit>'`. The contributor is pointed at the top of a 90-note directory rather than the one that is not readable.

EACCES ... scandir '<top dir>/<actual culprit>'`. The contributor is pointed at the top of a 90-note directory rather than the one that is not readable.

`packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-gate.mjs:112`

Evidence: A notes dir with a top-level note and an unreadable subdirectory:
$ chmod 000 /tmp/eacces/notes/locked
$ collectFailures('/tmp/eacces/notes')
[ 'cannot read /tmp/eacces/notes: EACCES: permission denied, scandir \'/tmp/eacces/notes/locked\'' ]
The message's subject, /tmp/eacces/notes, is readable; only the ENOENT/EACCES suffix names the directory that is not. The same misattribution applies to a subdirectory that disappears between the parent's readdir and its own.

Fix: Report the directory being entered — have the recursive walk throw a tagged error or catch per-directory inside the walk and surface the failing path. Alternatively narrow the guard to the top-level readdirSync call (the case AC-3 actually describes) and let a subdirectory error remain a throw.
